points.title: Verb „to be“
points.explanation: „to be“ wird je nach Person konjugiert: I am, you/we/they are, he/she/it is. Verneinung: is not / are not / am not.

points.title: Präsens (Present Simple)
points.explanation: Present Simple für Gewohnheiten. 3. Person Singular bekommt -s/-es: he works, she goes. Verneinung/Frage mit do/does.

points.title: Artikel (a, an, the)
points.explanation: „a“ vor Konsonantenklang, „an“ vor Vokalklang, „the“ für Bekanntes/Einzigartiges. Kein Artikel bei Plural/abstrakt allgemein.
examples: a book, an apple, the sun.

exercises.s: Ich habe ___ Auto. = I have ___ car.
Ich trinke Milch. = I drink ___ milk.
Sie liest ___ Buch. = She reads ___ book.

points.title: Pluralbildung
points.explanation: Regulär -s/-es (cats, boxes). Unregelmäßig: man→men, child→children, foot→feet, tooth→teeth. -y nach Konsonant → -ies.

points.title: there is / there are
points.explanation: „there is“ + Singular/unzählig, „there are“ + Plural. Verneinung: there is not / there are not; mit any in Frage/Verneinung.

exercises.s: Es gibt einen Hund. = ___ is a dog.
Es gibt zwei Autos. = There ___ two cars.

points.title: Possessive (’s, my, your)
points.explanation: ’s bei Personen (Tom’s car), of bei Dingen (the door of the room). Possessivpronomen: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.

exercises.s: Das Auto meines Vaters = my ___ car.
Der Name des Hundes = the name ___ the dog.
Toms und Annas Kinder = Tom and ___ children

points.title: Vergangenheit (Past Simple)
points.explanation: Regulär -ed (worked). Unregelmäßig: go→went, see→saw, have→had, do→did. Verneinung/Frage mit did + Infinitiv.

points.title: Present Perfect
points.explanation: have/has + past participle für Erfahrung/Ergebnis mit Gegenwart. Signalwörter: ever, never, already, yet, just, since, for.
examples: We have known him for years.

points.title: Komparativ & Superlativ
points.explanation: Kurz: -er/-est (taller, tallest). Lang: more/most (more expensive). Unregelmäßig: good→better→best, bad→worse→worst.

points.title: Modalverben (can, must, should)
points.explanation: can (Können/Erlaubnis), must (Pflicht), should (Empfehlung), have to (müssen). Nach Modalverb steht der Infinitiv ohne to.

points.title: Präpositionen (in, on, at)
points.explanation: Zeit: at (Uhrzeit), on (Tag/Tag+Datum), in (Monat/Jahr/Jahreszeit). Ort: at (Punkt), on (Fläche), in (umschlossen).

points.title: Zukunft (will / going to)
points.explanation: will + Infinitiv für spontane Entscheidungen/Vorhersagen. be going to für Pläne/absehbare Ereignisse.

exercises.s: Er plant zu reisen. = He ___ travel.
Spontane Entscheidung: I ___ (will) open the window.

points.title: Konditionalsätze Typ 1 & 2
points.explanation: Typ 1 (real): If + Present, will + Inf. Typ 2 (unreal): If + Past Simple, would + Inf. Komma, wenn if-Satz vorn.
examples: If it rains, I will stay.
If I were rich, I would travel.

exercises.s: If it rains, I ___ at home.
If I ___ rich, I would travel.
Typ 2: If he ___ (know), he would help.
If I ___ you, I would go.

points.title: Passiv (Passive Voice)
points.explanation: be + past participle. Tempus steckt in „be“: is made, was built, has been done. Täter mit „by“.
examples: The book is read by many.

points.title: Relativsätze (who, which, that)
points.explanation: who (Personen), which (Sachen), that (beide, im definierten Relativsatz). Non-defining mit Komma, „that“ nicht erlaubt.

exercises.s: Non-defining: mein Bruder, ___ in Rom lebt
Der Mann, dessen Auto … = the man ___ car …
Das Buch, das ich lese = the book ___ I read

points.title: Indirekte Rede
points.explanation: Zeitformen „backshiften“: Present→Past, Past→Past Perfect, will→would. Pronomen und Zeitwörter anpassen.
examples: “I am tired” → He said he was tired.
“I will go” → She said she would go.

exercises.s: “I am happy” → He said he ___ happy.
“I will call” → She said she ___ call.
“I saw it” → He said he ___ it.
“I have done it” → She said she ___ it.

points.title: Gerund vs. Infinitiv
points.explanation: Nach manchen Verben -ing (enjoy doing), nach anderen to (want to do). Nach Präpositionen immer -ing.

points.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
points.explanation: Past Simple = abgeschlossene Zeit (yesterday, in 2010). Present Perfect = offene Zeit/Erfahrung (ever, never, this week).

points.title: Konditionalsatz Typ 3 & gemischt
points.explanation: Typ 3 (unreal vergangen): If + Past Perfect, would have + p.p. Gemischt: If + Past Perfect, would + Inf (heutige Folge).
examples: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I had gone, I would be happy now.

exercises.s: If I ___ harder, I would have passed.
Typ 3: If she ___ (know), she would have come.
Gemischt (heutige Folge): If I had gone, I ___ happy now.
If they ___ (leave) earlier, they would have arrived.

points.title: Past Perfect
points.explanation: had + past participle für Vorzeitigkeit in der Vergangenheit. Oft mit when, after, before, by the time.
examples: When I arrived, the train had left.

exercises.s: She ___ the letter before he called.
By the time we came, they ___ (eat).

points.title: used to / would (Gewohnheit)
points.explanation: used to + Inf für vergangene Gewohnheiten/Zustände. would + Inf für vergangene Handlungen (nicht Zustände).

exercises.s: Früher spielten wir oft. = We ___ play.
Früher wohnte er hier. = He ___ live here.
„would“ für vergangene Gewohnheit geht NICHT bei
Früher hasste ich Spinat. = I ___ hate spinach.

points.title: Konjunktiv (subjunctive)
points.explanation: Nach suggest/insist/recommend + that: Infinitiv ohne -s (I suggest he go). „If I were …“ (irreal). „It’s essential that she be …“.
examples: It’s vital that she be present.

exercises.s: If I ___ you, I would go.
I insist that she ___ the truth.

points.title: Textkonnektoren (however, although)
points.explanation: Konzessiv: although, however, despite + -ing/Nomen. Kausal: because, since, due to. Final: so that, in order to.
examples: Although it rained, we went out.
He studies hard so that he passes.

exercises.s: Grund: ___ it was late, we left.

points.title: Phrasal Verbs
points.explanation: Verb + Partikel mit eigener Bedeutung: give up (aufgeben), look after (aufpassen), put off (verschieben), find out (herausfinden).
